newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish minister slams Skandia/Stadshypotek plan.
newsitem.headline: Swedish minister slams Skandia/Stadshypotek plan.

text.p: Swedish Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said on Monday he was strongly critical of the proposed plan by insurer Skandia and mortgage lender Stadshypotek to merge.

He said he had no confidence in Stadshypotek's board. The state holds a 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek. Asbrink said the government's original plan of a controlled auction to dispose of its 34 percent stake in Stadshypotek was still valid.

"I am very critical ofhow the board of directors of Stadshypotek has handled this question. I recently learned that the board has been negotiating with Skandia regarding a merger for some time without informing the largest shareholder (the state).

"In my opinion the Stadshypotek board has clearly gone into the area reserved for shareholders. The board's behaviour is contrary to what is customary practice in Swedish industry," Asbrink said in a statement.
"I also find it remarkable that the Board of Directors, after it was informed of the government's strategy for selling the state's shares, supports Skandia to present a public bid now.
"It is only an auction process which could determine the best price for the shares. The auction process could suffer as a result of the board's behaviour," he said.
"Therefore, I have no confidence in the present Board of Directors of Stadshypotek," he added.
Skandia and Stadshypotek said earlier they planned to merge to create the Nordic region's largest financial services company.
The two companies said efforts to discuss the merger with the finance ministry had been fruitless. -- Simon Haydon, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700-1004
